newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar sinks below 111 yen amid trade jitters.
newsitem.headline: Dollar sinks below 111 yen amid trade jitters.

text.p: The dollar slipped to its lowest level against the yen in almost seven months on Wednesday, sinking to 110.97 yen in Tokyo as a sharp rise in Japan's sensitive current account surplus fuelled worries over trade tension.
The dip below 111 yen took the dollar to its lowest level since November 20, 1996.

The dollar was temporarily lifted in the morning after the release of trade figures which were mostly in line with market expectations, but it soon resumed its downward march on worries over renewed U.S.-Japan trade friction, dealers said.

The worries were aggravated by remarks from U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, who said that Japan should foster demand-led recovery at home and avoid running up external surpluses that would hurt global growth.

Traders are speculating that the Japanese government will have to let the yen climb in order to keep its ballooning trade surplus in check ahead of the meeting of the world's seven leading industrialised nations in Denver later this month.

The dollar closed at 112.17/22 yen in New York on Tuesday. On Wednesday morning, Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) announced that the surplus in the current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, rose 92.7 percent to 1.09 trillion yen ($9.8 billion) in April from a year earlier.
